name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 182 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 25% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 182 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 25 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Lateef Bhat, a Lashkar-e-Taiba commander, was killed in a Kulgam encounter and his weapon was recovered, prompting Amit Shah to declare Kashmir free of locally recruited terrorists. A military vehicle accident in Manipur killed an army captain and injured three soldiers, leading the governor and chief minister to pay tribute. The Kashmir chief minister announced faster digital reforms, a paperless cabinet and stronger cyber security. India and Japan deepened defence and security ties at a 2+2 meeting, expanding cooperation. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Lateef Bhat, en Lashkar-e‑Taiba-kommandør, ble drept i et oppgjør i Kulgam, og våpenet hans ble funnet, noe som fikk Amit Shah til å erklære Kashmir fritt for lokalt rekrutterte terrorister. En militærkjøretøyulykke i Manipur drepte en hærkaptein og såret tre soldater, og guvernøren og statsministeren holdt en hyllest. Kashmir-statsministeren kunngjorde raskere digitale reformer, et papirfritt kabinett og sterkere cybersikkerhet. India og Japan styrket forsvars‑ og sikkerhetsbåndene i et 2+2‑møte, og utvidet samarbeidet. 437 dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
